properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): a design has exactly ONE measurement root, derived from the folder its store sits in and recorded nowhere — req:persistence's in-repo layout, dropped 2026-09-25, surviving in wall_check::project_root — so every file in a sibling code repo reads outside_root; neither the #609 pointer nor the hosted door changes that, and three reports reached nothing because intake is pull and the class's open ideas are scheduled nowhere
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL on Anthony's word, 2026-09-28 ("As is the rule for feedback, please /root-cause all issues and /brainstorm all ideas"), on art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27, entries of 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24 (twice, the second titled "third report").

① OBSERVED (dev_storyflow sessions 0c19a800 and 3bd108ab; the design in dev_storyflow, the code in the sibling ../storyflow): link_artifact on `../storyflow/...` returned `basis: none, why: outside_root` / `not_measured: outside_root` — five registrations over three sessions, none with a baseline. Expected: a baseline, so a later edit shows as drift. NOT affected: files under the design repo's own folder are measured and their edits are reported.

② PRECEDENT, searched on the raw words (`outside_root`, `not_measured`, "sibling repo", "extra roots"). The class is on record three times already: dec:idea-how-is-a-source-outside-the-repo-registered (2026-08-11, a sibling-repo source broke CI and was backed out), fact:the-out-of-tree-notion-exists-but-is-keyed-on-the-path-shape-and-only-one-instrument-honours-it and fact:an-out-of-tree-artifact-registration-passed-locally-as-unmeasurable-and-failed-ci-as-missing (2026-09-21: flo2's twelve, and this design's own registration, also backed out), with dec:idea-how-does-an-artifact-say-it-belongs-to-another-repository still open. The two-instrument half was fixed 2026-09-23 (chg:the-server-and-the-gate-share-one-meaning-for-an-artifact-location). The storyflow reports are occurrences four to six of a known class, not a new one.

③ CANDIDATES, from the bones:
 A (intent / allocation): one root, derived from where the store sits. wall_check::project_root maps `<root>/.reflow2/graph` → `<root>`, measure.rs refuses anything outside it, and the only override (--tree-root) swaps in another SINGLE root. That is req:persistence's layout ("the graph lives at ./.reflow2/graph inside the consumer project"), dropped 2026-09-25, still in the code.
 B (the reporter's path form): the `../` form is at fault; an absolute path or --tree-root would measure.
 C (contract / governance): the refusal is the deliberate root bound (graph text must never direct a read) working as designed; the real gap is that the reply offers no route to a baseline.
 D (outside the suspect component): intake and planning. The reports never reached anything that schedules work.
 E: the observation is wrong (an older binary, or the wrong thing measured).

④ WHAT WOULD REFUTE EACH: A is refuted if any configuration lets ONE design measure a file in its own folder AND one in a sibling without rewriting locations. B is refuted if the absolute and --tree-root forms also leave one tree out. C is refuted if an asserted baseline makes the server's own sweep detect a sibling edit. E is refuted if 0.72.0 gives the same reply.

⑤ TAKEN on the 0.72.0 release binary, in a scratch two-sibling layout (design-repo/.reflow2/graph beside code-repo/), one-shot --call from cwd=/tmp. The root comes from the graph path, not the cwd.
 · `../code-repo/src/main.rs` → `basis: none, not_measured {why: outside_root}`. E REFUTED: exact reproduction.
 · The absolute path to the same file → outside_root. `docs/note.md` in the design folder → measured.
 · --tree-root at the common parent: the sibling measures only when re-registered as `code-repo/src/main.rs`, and the design folder's own `docs/note.md` then reads missing_artifact. B REFUTED: every form leaves one of the two trees outside the root. A SURVIVES. The CLI has no multi-root option, and #609's pointer (run from the branch's debug build) REFUSES a `roots` key at startup: "unknown field `roots`, expected `design` or `also`". `[[also]]` names designs, not trees.
 · Link with a caller checksum → `basis: asserted`. Then both files were edited. A no-argument reconcile_artifacts listed the sibling under `unmeasurable` with no finding, and gave the design-folder edit as checksum_change. Only reconcile_artifacts with a caller-hashed `observed` found the sibling edit. C PARTLY HOLDS: a manual route exists, and it is exactly the hand-hashing measure.rs was built to end. The outside_root sentence never mentions it, though the no_tree sentence does ("pass the checksum to assert it, or reconcile with `observed`").
 · Hosted door, with a local --registry-root --http server of the same version standing in for api.flo2.io's engine: BOTH locations answer `no_tree`. The asymmetry vanishes because nothing is measured at all.

⑥ CLASS: THE DESIGN ASSUMES DESIGN AND CODE SHARE ONE ROOT. It derives that root from where its store sits and never records it. Every out-of-tree occurrence since 2026-08-11 is this class, and a declared, multi-tree measurement would have stopped all of them. Does #609 or the hosted door change it? NO. The pointer moves the root to the code folder, which is good for a one-repo implementation, and by design names designs, not trees. The hosted engine has no root. The planned client (epoch:planned-local-files-are-measured-for-a-remote-design, combined position 7) measures "a folder's OWN files", which is one root again. Locations written under the old root (`../storyflow/...` from dev_storyflow) become escapes from the new one.

WHY THREE REPORTS REACHED NOTHING, measured in three parts. (1) INTAKE IS PULL: the reports sat in dev_storyflow's own reflow2_feedback.md. The previous copy was triaged 2026-09-08 and this one 2026-09-28, so for 20 days nothing in reflow2 could see them. (2) EVEN ARRIVED, THEY HAD NOTHING TO ATTACH TO THAT SCHEDULES WORK. Both open ideas on the class are `proposed` with no SCHEDULED_FOR or epoch edge. The accepted dec:idea-a-design-apart-from-its-code-knows-where-its-implementation-is says "out-of-tree measurement fixed first" only in prose, and the 12-increment combined plan agreed 2026-09-27 has no increment for it. (3) REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN NEVER CARRIES THE CASE: of its 472 Artifacts, 471 are relative in-tree and 1 is a URI, with 0 absolute and 0 `../`. Both out-of-tree registrations it attempted were backed out to keep CI green, so the maintainer's own instrument never shows the gap.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: HELD. The reply shape is verbatim on 0.72.0, there is no baseline, drift is undetectable by the server's own sweep, and this applies to every code artifact in a two-repo layout. REFINED: a caller-asserted checksum plus a caller-hashed `observed` does catch drift. That route is manual, and the refusal does not name it.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE for this triage (no fix). A class-pinning test would assert: one design, two sibling trees declared by whatever mechanism is chosen; a file in each is measured on link; an edit to the sibling file comes back checksum_change from a no-argument reconcile_artifacts, from loop_status and from the CI gate alike; the verdicts survive export → import into another folder; and an outside-the-root refusal names the assert/observed route.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED. api.flo2.io itself was not called (a local registry of the same version stood in, and flo2's gateway could differ). The storyflow design on flo2 was not read, so how its existing `../storyflow/...` locations read today is inferred from source. The #609 behaviour was measured on the branch's debug build as it stands before merge.
